reply_text:
I found four dated AI predictions Musk made in 2022 and one remark about AI that has no date. Two cautions before you check them. The interview quotes come from a fan-made transcript, not TED's own. The AGI tweet and the robot tweet I read only as tweets embedded in a news article, because X would not open.

- **AGI by 2029:** On 30 May 2022 he tweeted "2029 feels like a pivotal year. I'd be surprised if we don't have AGI by then." I read it embedded in a TNW article from 3 June 2022.
- **Self-driving solved in 2022:** In the TED interview with Chris Anderson (recorded 6 April 2022, published 18 April), he said "I actually am confident that we will solve it this year." TED's own page opened, but the transcript text didn't load, so these quotes come from a fan site.
- **Optimus robot timeline:** In the same interview he said "something useful next year, but I think, quite likely within at least two years." He also said robots for the home would come "in less than ten years." These are humanoid-robot forecasts, so whether they count as "AI" is your call. The same goes for the June 2022 tweet that a working Optimus prototype might be ready by AI Day on 30 September.

Pages that opened but held nothing usable:
- Rev's transcript of the April 2022 earnings call cut off during the opening remarks. Musk's comments on self-driving were missing.
- I didn't keep the text of that page between steps, so nothing from it is quoted.
- TheStreet's write-up of AI Day 2022 had only excerpts, including "it will walk in a few weeks." I left that out because "a few weeks" is too vague a timeframe.

The widely reported AI Day forecast that Optimus would reach customers in "3 to 5 years" showed up only in a search result snippet. I didn't open a page with it, so it isn't listed. I used 7 of 12 searches and all 6 page openings. I stopped searching because I couldn't open any more pages to quote from.
